title: Minimum Moves to Equal Array Elements II
summary: For an integer array of size n, determine the least number of moves needed to make all elements identical.
statement: For an integer array of size n, determine the least number of moves needed to make all elements identical. Each move allows increasing or decreasing any element by one. Ensure the solution fits within a 32-bit integer.
constraints: 1 <= nums.length <= 100,000; -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9; the answer fits a signed 32-bit integer.
One move increments OR decrements exactly one entry by 1. Return the fewest moves to make all entries equal.
This differs from incrementing n-1 entries per move; any median is an optimal target.
hints: Moving every value to target t costs the sum of its absolute distances from t.
Pair the smallest and largest values; any target between them has the same cost for that pair.
Sort, choose a middle value, and sum absolute differences from it.
The nested pair intervals meet at a median. For even lengths any point between the middle two is optimal.
editorial: Absolute-distance cost decreases toward a median and increases after passing it. Pairing extremes gives another proof: each pair pays at least its gap, and a median achieves every pair lower bound simultaneously. The oracle tries every integer target in small input ranges.

tests.explanation: Increment 1 to 2 and decrement 3 to 2: two single-entry moves suffice.
Target 1 costs 9 moves. Targeting the mean, 4, would cost 3+3+6=12.
